sentences.text: Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is the first application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail to the applicant/accused, relating to FIR/Crime No.195/2023 dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station Chimanganj Mandi, District Ujjain (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376, 376(2)(N), 368 and 34 of IPC along with Sections 3/4 and 5(L)/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2 . Prosecution story in brief is that at the time of incident, prosecutrix was below 16 years of age.
As per the report, on the date of incident 2 MCRC-19626-2024 prosecutrix was in her house cooking food and after sometime complainant / mother found the prosecutrix missing.
She unsuccessfully tried to search her everywhere.

Thereafter, she lodged an FIR and expressed her doubt upon the Suraj@ Judda vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132583154/
1 applicant that he must had abducted her daughter.

entities.text: Suraj@ Judda vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: During the investigation, it has been found that present applicant has abducted and took the minor prosecutrix with him and had committed rape upon her.
On the basis of aforesaid, the crime has been registered.
3 . Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant has not committed the offence and he has falsely been implicated in the case.
He is in jail since 23.06.2023.
There is no evidence available on record to connect the applicant with the aforesaid crime.

After completion of investigation,
charge- sheet has been filed.
Prosecutrix (PW-3) has been examined before the trial Court and she has not supported the case of prosecution.
He is a permanent resident of Ujjain and there is no possibility that after release he will abscond and temper with the evidence.
Trial will take considerable long time for its disposal therefore, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.

4 . On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has objected the prayer and prayed for its rejection.
5.

Having considered the rival submissions and after perusal of the case diary so also considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also looking to the fact that prosecutrix has turned hostile before the trial Court, therefore, this Court is of the view that applicant deserve to be enlarged on bail, hence, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant- Suraj @ Judda shall be released on bail 3 MCRC-19626-2024 on his furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Court, for his appearance before the concerned Court regularly on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during trial.

It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437 (3) of Cr. P. C.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of trial but in case of bail jump, it shall become ineffective.
8. With the aforesaid, this application is allowed and stand disposed off.
Certified copy, as per Rules.
